**Observations from the image:**
- A stem section is shown laid flat on newspaper
- There is a large, dark brown to almost black lesion/canker at a node on the stem
- The lesion appears sunken and irregularly shaped around the node
- Leaves at the affected node are completely dead (brown, withered, and desiccated)
- No visible white/gray fungal growth (ruling out Gray Mold, Sclerotinia, Southern Blight)
- No fluffy mycelium or spore masses visible
- The stem tissue appears darkened and necrotic at the canker site

**Reasoning:**
The key features here are the very dark brown to almost black stem canker, irregular shape, and associated dead leaf tissue at the node. This closely matches **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**, which is described as "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers" on stems. The absence of white fungal mats rules out Southern Blight and Sclerotinia. The absence of gray fuzzy sporulation rules out Gray Mold. Late blight stem lesions are typically lighter brown and less well-defined without this level of blackening. The canker here has the characteristic dark coloration and stem location described for Alternaria stem canker.
